solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quite a swell, displaying extremes of style continuously

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are wanted

parts.note: first and last letters of style
as in 'talk away', doing something without stopping

explanation.surface: A dandy whose stylishness never lapses is quite a swell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like a fashionable person; here it is the heaving of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaway is a rough sea with a heavy swell running, so quite a swell describes it.

clue.text: Government historically showing wisdom about rent

indicators.note: one word goes about, that is around, the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a rent is a tear in cloth

explanation.surface: An old regime shows good sense over the matter of rents.
explanation.walkthrough: STEARAGE is an obsolete spelling of steerage, which once meant governing or direction, as in steering a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage, here in an archaic spelling, formerly meant direction or management of affairs, i.e. governance.

clue.text: Not properly hearty, I (right obvious inside), losing red blood cells

definitions.note: describes the condition rather than naming it

indicators.note: something not done properly is disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: open as in plain to see

explanation.surface: A patient admits to feeling below par while plainly losing blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket just places R and OPEN beside I within the fodder; all twelve letters are then mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Erythropenia is a medical deficiency of red blood cells, the state of having lost them.

clue.text: Nuts: kilo consumed in Texas town

indicators.note: what is consumed ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Waco is a city in central Texas
K is the abbreviation for kilo

explanation.surface: A kilo of nuts gets eaten in a small Texan town.
explanation.definitionFit: Wacko is slang for crazy, the same informal sense as nuts.

clue.text: Resurrection unaltered after Satan's mistreatment

indicators.note: mistreatment roughs up the word beside it, so its letters are knocked out of order
after places one piece behind the other in the finished word

parts.note: the five letters of the devil's name, rearranged

explanation.surface: A resurrection follows the torments Satan inflicted, a near-theological scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Satan is read as 'has', a mere join.
explanation.definitionFit: Anastasis is Greek for rising up, the name given to the resurrection, especially Christ's harrowing of hell in art.

clue.text: Gland, one included in examinations

indicators.note: to be included in something is to sit inside it

explanation.surface: A gland gets checked as part of a set of medical examinations.
explanation.definitionFit: The testis is the male reproductive gland that produces sperm.

clue.text: Some disco music? Echt dancing number

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and change places

parts.note: the German word for genuine, rearranged
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A genuine dance number is the sort of thing a disco plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Echt, borrowed from German, means authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: Techno is a style of electronic dance music played in clubs, so it is one kind of disco music, hence the question mark.

clue.text: The old served special cuppas with qualified teacher?

indicators.note: a special version is a made-up variant, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: cups of tea, with the letters rearranged
DEd, Doctor of Education, a teaching qualification

explanation.surface: In bygone days special cups of tea were served to a trained teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks an obsolete word: stead once meant to help or serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Stead, now obsolete as a verb, meant to be of use or service to someone, so steaded is served.

clue.text: Like raw fish one's served in hellish place once

indicators.note: a dish served in something is placed inside it

parts.note: tartare describes raw minced fish or meat dishes

explanation.surface: A raw-fish dish is dished up in some infernal spot of old.
explanation.walkthrough: TARTARIE is Spenser's form of Tartarus, the classical underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartarus is the hell of Greek myth; Tartarie is an archaic form, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Dividing plots I'll separate design

indicators.note: to separate something is to come between its parts, splitting it open around the inserted letters

parts.note: an intent is a purpose or design
plural of erf, a South African plot of land

explanation.surface: A schemer threatens to split up plots and plans.
explanation.walkthrough: An erf is a South African term for a small plot of ground, with an irregular plural; the inserted letters come after the third letter of the design word.
explanation.definitionFit: Intervenient means coming between, so it is a formal synonym of dividing.

clue.text: Side-slip was in sport including such a manoeuvre

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a past tense form of ski, spelt with an apostrophe-free variant

explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives ski'd as a past tense of ski; skiing being a sport that includes side-slips, the tail adds the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a sideways slide out of control, while the same letters spell a past tense of the verb to ski.

clue.text: Vagrant once having to peddle round for all to see

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: trant is an old dialect verb meaning to hawk goods
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: An old-time tramp has to hawk his wares in public.
explanation.walkthrough: Truant formerly meant an idle wanderer or vagabond, not just a pupil skipping school.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage a truant was an idler or vagabond, which matches a vagrant of former times.

clue.text: Public drain smelled awful

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dialect noun for a ditch or drain
second meaning: past tense of a verb for giving off a bad odour

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about a smelly drain; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stank is a Scots and dialect word for a pond or drain, and also the past tense of stink.

clue.text: A beauty, awfully cheery etc, captivates one

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, leaving the letters in a mess
to captivate is literally to hold captive, keeping something inside

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A beauty whose bubbly chatter and so on charms everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-catcher is something or someone striking to look at, so a beauty fits.

clue.text: Musteline, all right after a bit of a kip

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first in the answer

parts.note: the at is a Laotian coin, one hundredth of a kip

explanation.surface: A weasel-like creature is fine after a short nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kip' suggests a nap; it is the currency of Laos, divided into 100 at.
explanation.definitionFit: The atok is a South American skunk, and skunks were once classed with weasels in the musteline family.

clue.text: Excitement in most of yield being trimmed

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: the heat of the moment is excitement

explanation.surface: A tense moment while the harvest is cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimmed' is slang for fleeced, swindled, not cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim someone is informal for cheating them out of money, so trimmed equals cheated.

clue.text: Tap overspread ground right away

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reduced and remixed
something sent away is gone, so that letter is removed

explanation.surface: A tap covered the ground, but the right side was washed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tap' is the wiretap sense, listening in secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap a phone is to listen in secretly, which is what eavesdropping means.

clue.text: Glowing round head of chrysanthemum, rooting from the stem

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one goes around the other
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A glowing flower whose head is a chrysanthemum puts out roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicant is a botanical term for a plant that sends out roots from its stem, as ivy does.

clue.text: Senior officers love having sailors around

indicators.note: around means surrounding, with the other piece enclosed

parts.note: nada is nothing, and love is nil in tennis

explanation.surface: High-ranking officers adore being surrounded by seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanadar was the officer in charge of an Indian police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanadars were Indian police officers in charge of a station, senior to the constables under them.

clue.text: Emphasizes troubles, not half dire

indicators.note: not means the following letters are excluded from the word

parts.note: distresses means troubles, as a verb

explanation.surface: A speaker dwells on problems while insisting they are only moderately serious.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasize it, so stresses and emphasizes are synonyms.

clue.text: Native American having to knock entering dry house

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members stay dry

explanation.surface: A Native American must knock before going into a house where alcohol is banned.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry here means teetotal, which AA stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Spicy pastry dish sale included

indicators.note: something included is held within the other piece

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish
cant is an old word for an auction or sale

explanation.surface: A savoury pie is offered at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Picante is the Spanish for hot or piquant, used of spicy sauces.

clue.text: More piping setting back river that is between two others?

indicators.note: between means flanked on both sides by the other piece

parts.note: two more rivers, R being the abbreviation

indicators.note: setting something back turns it the other way, so it reads in reverse

parts.note: the Dee is a British river

explanation.surface: A river squeezed between two others is diverted back, getting more like a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piping' suggests a pipe for water; here it is the reedy, thin quality of a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A piping voice is high and thin, as is a reedy one, so more piping means reedier.

clue.text: Buck lives in tranquillity

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

explanation.surface: A male deer lives a peaceful life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' looks like a deer; it is the verb, as in buck the trend.
explanation.definitionFit: To buck a trend or rule is to oppose it, so buck is a synonym for resist.

clue.text: Who'll flog rice and pies?

indicators.note: to flog is to beat, and beaten letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A question asking who might sell rice and pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' means sell for the whole clue and beat for the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Épicier is French for a grocer, and grocers sell staples like rice and pies.

clue.text: Grand family of bays (not US) in boggy Scottish ground

indicators.note: not means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: Laurus is the botanical genus of bay trees

explanation.surface: A grand family of horses, none American, kept on wet Scottish land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bays' suggests horses; they are bay laurel trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaur is Scots for mud or mire, the stuff of boggy ground.

clue.text: Game bird, busy one wrapping large chest, avoided by one

indicators.note: wrapping means enclosing the other piece
what is avoided is left out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a cassone is a large Italian chest

explanation.surface: A game bird, ever busy, guards a big chest it avoids.
explanation.walkthrough: A cassone is an ornate Italian marriage chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bécasse is French for the woodcock, a game bird, and Chambers lists it as a word for it.

clue.text: Catch on the river bottom, soft

parts.note: a bum is the bottom, British slang

explanation.surface: Fishing, someone snags the riverbed and finds it soft.
explanation.walkthrough: In bumps races at Oxford and Cambridge, rowing crews try to catch and touch the boat ahead, a bump.
explanation.definitionFit: In bumping races a crew that catches the boat in front scores a bump, so it is a catch made on the river.

clue.text: Floral decorations, a feature of Belle Isle

indicators.note: a feature of something is a part of it, so the letters lie within the phrase

explanation.surface: Flower garlands are a feature of an island resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Leis are Hawaiian garlands of flowers, worn as decorations around the neck.

clue.text: Sea winds, darn sea winds catching little bird

indicators.note: the verb winds, twisting things round, so the letters are coiled into a new order
catching means holding the other piece within

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A sailor curses the winds at sea that blow a small bird about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' appears twice: the noun is the definition, the second, read as a verb, signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Antitrades are winds blowing above and opposite to the trade winds over the oceans.

clue.text: Before end of day Scots aim for camp

indicators.note: before puts one piece in front of the other

parts.note: mint is Scots for to aim or attempt

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Before nightfall the Scots set their sights on the camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like tents; it is the adjective for theatrical, effeminate manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Minty is old slang for effeminate or homosexual, the same sense as camp.

clue.text: Dry chalk bed, mostly scorched round middle of October

indicators.note: round means surrounding the other piece
mostly means all but the last letter
the middle of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A dry chalky streambed, largely parched around mid-October.
explanation.definitionFit: A bourne is a stream on chalk downland that runs only in wet seasons, leaving a dry bed otherwise.

clue.text: 'Ingenious' or 'spot-on' captures X

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold inside

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Two words in quotes are offered as alternatives, one captured by a mystery X.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent in the sense of a clever contrivance, as in a patent method, means ingenious.

clue.text: Whale-catchers maybe folded waterproof sheet on board

indicators.note: folding a sheet doubles it back on itself, so the word runs the other way
on board means inside a ship, the abbreviation for steamship around the other piece

parts.note: on board conventionally means placed inside SS, a steamship

explanation.surface: Whalers fold a tarpaulin aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'a sprat to catch a whale' (or mackerel) means a small outlay to win something big.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'throw a sprat to catch a whale' makes sprats the small bait that catches whales.
